hook: Contract staff at Gandhi, Osmania protest for *₹26,000* minimum wage
hook_b: Contract staff at Gandhi, Osmania protest for *₹26,000* minimum wage
tldr: Sanitation, patient care and security contract workers at government hospitals across Telangana protested for a second day on Friday.

beats.what: Leader M Narasimha said workers lack statutory minimum wages, paid leave, bonuses and even new uniforms, per Telangana Today.
beats.why: The Telangana Medical Contract Employees and Workers Union says it has sought a ₹26,000 minimum monthly wage for two years.
beats.care: Protests were held at Gandhi, Osmania General, Niloufer, Fever, King Koti, Koti Maternity, Malakpet Area, Nampally and Sarojini Devi Eye hospitals.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Day 2 of statewide protests by sanitation, patient-care and security staff.

facts.t: Protests reached *9* Hyderabad hospitals including Gandhi, Osmania and Niloufer.

viz.verdict: Patients could be hit if a strike goes ahead, per the union's warning

watch: Whether the government calls the union for talks before a teaching-hospital strike.

fact: Contract hospital workers protest a second day, seeking a *₹26,000* monthly minimum wage.
twist: The union warns of a *massive strike* in all teaching hospitals if the state does not act.
